source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

35051.t:
Sierra County stayed with the Republican in New Mexico's U.S. Senate race, but by far less than in 2024. Marker won 2,433 votes to Luján's 2,327, a margin of about 2 points, after Trump carried the county by 19. That is a 17-point move toward the Democrats, a little smaller than the typical New Mexico county's 19 and above the national typical move of 14. It ranked 24th of 33 in the state, where every county moved left.

Turnout was 80% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar counties moved further: Luna by 33 points, Hidalgo by 27 and Colfax by 22, all flipping to Luján.

35041.t:
Roosevelt County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by a narrower margin than in 2024. Marker beat Luján 3,054 to 1,733, a margin of 28 points, down from Trump's 43-point win over Harris. That is a 16-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical New Mexico county's 19-point shift, ranking 27th of 33 in a state where every county moved left and Luján won by 27 points. Similar Republican counties moved somewhat more: Curry and Torrance each shifted 19 points and Quay 17.

Only 4,787 votes were cast, 72% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35011.t:
De Baca County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker, but by less than in 2024. Marker won 513 votes to Luján's 227, a margin of 39 points, down from Trump's 51-point margin over Harris. That is a 12-point move toward the Democrats. Turnout was 740 votes, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

Every county in New Mexico moved left, and De Baca moved less than most, ranking 32nd of 33. The typical county shifted 19 points, and the state as a whole went from a 6-point Harris margin to a 27-point Luján win. Similar small, heavily Republican counties moved further: Union 17 points, Catron 16, Harding 16. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

35055.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Democrat Luján carried Taos County by 67 points over Republican Marker, 11,236 votes to 2,238. Harris won it by 48 points in 2024, so the county moved 19 points toward the Democrats. That is almost exactly the typical New Mexico county, which moved 19, and ranks 16th of 33 in the state. All 33 shifted left. The national typical move was 14 points.

Turnout fell: 13,474 votes were cast, 81% of the 16,636 in 2024, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Santa Fe moved 15 points, Los Alamos 10 and San Miguel 24.

35021.t:
Harding County, New Mexico's smallest by votes cast, stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 39 points in 2024; this time Marker beat Luján 232 to 143, a 24-point margin on 375 votes. That is a 16-point shift left, a bit less than the typical New Mexico county's 19 points and ranking 28th of 33. Every county in the state moved left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

Turnout was 87% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar Republican counties moved comparably: Quay 17 points, Torrance 19, Lincoln 13.

35015.t:
Eddy County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved toward the Democrats. Marker (R) carried it 11,195 to 4,955 over Luján (D), a 39-point margin, down from Trump's 56-point win over Harris in 2024. That is a 17-point shift, slightly smaller than the typical New Mexico county's 19 points, where every county moved left, and larger than the typical 14 points nationally. Nearby Lea moved 24 points and Chaves 19.

Turnout fell sharply: 16,150 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Statewide, Luján won by 27 points.

35017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Grant County gave Democrat Ben Luján a 25-point win over Republican Larry Marker, 7,237 votes to 4,309. Kamala Harris carried it by 5 points in 2024, so the county moved 20 points toward the Democrats. That nearly matches the statewide shift of 20 points and is slightly more than the typical New Mexico county's 19. It ranks 15th of 33 counties by move. Among similar counties, Cibola and Socorro moved more, by 27 and 28 points, while Sandoval moved 14.

The county cast 11,546 votes, 81% of its 2024 total of 14,224. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35057.t:
Torrance County stayed Republican in the U.S. Senate race but by about half its 2024 margin. Marker beat Luján 3,269 to 2,203, a margin of 20 points, after Trump carried the county over Harris by 38. That is a 19-point move toward the Democrats, almost exactly the typical move among New Mexico counties, all 33 of which shifted left, and above the national typical move of 14 points. It moved more than the similar counties of Lincoln (13), Quay (17) and Roosevelt (16).

Turnout was 5,472 votes, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

35059.t:
Union County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but moved about 17 points toward the Democrats. Marker beat Luján 859 to 410, a margin of 35 points, down from Trump's 52-point win over Harris in 2024. About 98% of the expected vote is counted.

Every New Mexico county moved left, the typical one by 19 points, and Union ranks 25th of 33. Similar strongly Republican counties moved by comparable amounts: De Baca by 12 points, Catron by 16 and Eddy by 17. Only 1,269 votes were cast, about 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35035.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Otero County moved about 19 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 27 points in 2024. This time Marker won it by 8, with 9,726 votes to Luján's 8,273. That shift matches the typical New Mexico county, all 33 of which moved left, and is a little smaller than the state's 21-point swing toward Luján. Comparable Republican-leaning counties moved further: San Juan by 22 points, Valencia by 23 and Luna by 33. Valencia and Luna both flipped to Luján.

Only 17,999 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35027.t:
Lincoln County stayed solidly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but swung toward the Democrats. Marker won 4,804 votes to Luján's 2,844, a 26-point margin, down from Trump's 39-point win in 2024. That 13-point shift toward the Democrats was smaller than in most of New Mexico: the county ranked 31st of 33, where the typical county moved 19 points and the state as a whole moved more than 20 as Luján won by 27. Similar Republican counties moved further, including Torrance and Curry (19 points each) and Quay (17).

Turnout fell sharply. The 7,648 votes cast were 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35005.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker, Chaves County stayed Republican but by a much smaller margin than in 2024. Marker won 9,755 votes to Luján's 5,721, a 26-point margin, down from Trump's 45-point margin over Harris. That is a 19-point move toward the Democrats, matching the typical New Mexico county and close to the state's 21-point shift. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points. Among similar counties, Curry moved about as much (19 points), Roosevelt slightly less (16) and Lincoln less (13).

Turnout was 15,476 votes, 70% of the 22,200 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35043.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker, Sandoval County voted Democratic by 19 points, 38,766 to 26,187, up from Harris's 6-point edge in 2024. That 14-point shift toward the Democrats matches the typical county nationally but is among the smallest in New Mexico: Sandoval ranks 30th of 33 counties by move, while the typical county there swung 19 points and the state as a whole went from D+6 to D+27. Comparable counties moved further, including Doña Ana at 26 points, Grant at 20 and Cibola at 27.

About 64,953 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35061.t: Valencia County voted for Trump by 16 points in 2024 and for Democrat Ben Luján by 6 points over Republican Larry Marker in the 2026 Senate race, 13,921 votes to 12,229. That 23-point swing toward the Democrats makes it one of five New Mexico counties to flip from Trump to the Democrat. It moved somewhat more than the state as a whole (about 21 points) and the typical New Mexico county (19), and well above the national norm of 14. Among similar counties, Colfax moved about the same (22), Luna moved more (33) and Sierra less (17). Turnout was 79% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot show who changed their mind and who stayed home.

35019.t:
Guadalupe County swung harder than any other county in New Mexico in the U.S. Senate race. Harris carried it by less than a point in 2024; this time Luján beat Marker 1,030 to 468, a 37-point margin and a 37-point move toward the Democrats. Every New Mexico county moved left, the typical one by 19 points, and similar counties moved less: Cibola by 27 points, Socorro by 28 and Grant by 20.

Only 1,498 votes were cast, 77% of the 1,938 cast in 2024. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35028.t:
Los Alamos County moved 10 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, where Luján beat Marker by 6,927 votes to 2,949, a 40-point margin, up from Harris's 30-point margin over Trump in 2024. All 33 New Mexico counties moved left, and Los Alamos moved the least. The typical county shifted 19 points and the state about 21. Comparable counties went much further: San Miguel 24 points, Rio Arriba 27 and McKinley 33. Nationally, the typical move was 14 points.

The county cast 9,876 votes, 81% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35053.t:
Socorro County flipped. Trump carried it by 4 points in 2024, but in the U.S. Senate race Luján beat Marker here by 24 points, 3,602 votes to 2,187. That 28-point swing toward the Democrats is the fifth-largest among New Mexico's 33 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county shifted 19 points and the state as a whole 21. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Cibola by 27 points and Colfax by 22, while Guadalupe swung 37.

About 5,789 votes were cast, roughly 80% of the 2024 total of 7,233. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell how much of the swing came from people changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

35049.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Santa Fe County gave Luján (D) 57,795 votes to Marker's (R) 12,699, a 64-point Democratic margin, up from Kamala Harris's 49-point margin in 2024. That 15-point shift toward the Democrats was smaller than the statewide swing of 21 points and the typical New Mexico county's 19. Santa Fe ranked 29th of 33 counties by move, though second by votes cast. Among similar counties, Taos moved 19 points and San Miguel 24, while Los Alamos moved 10.

Turnout fell: 70,494 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35006.t:
Cibola County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker. Harris carried it by 2 points in 2024; Luján won it by 29, 4,660 votes to 2,575. That 27-point move outpaced the statewide shift of 21 points and ranks seventh of New Mexico's 33 counties, all of which moved left. The typical New Mexico county moved 19 points, and the typical county nationally moved 14.

Turnout fell to 81% of the 2024 level, 7,235 votes against 8,977, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Grant moved 20 points, Socorro 28, and Guadalupe 37.

35047.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, San Miguel County gave Luján 6,831 votes to Marker's 2,164, a Democratic margin of 52 points. Harris carried it by 28 points in 2024, so the county moved 24 points toward the Democrats. That is more than the state's 21-point shift and the typical New Mexico county's 19. It ranks 10th of 33 counties by move, and every county in the state moved left.

Turnout was 8,995 votes, 81% of the 11,108 cast in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Los Alamos moved 10 points, Rio Arriba 27 and McKinley 33.

35039.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Rio Arriba County gave Democrat Luján 9,270 votes to Republican Marker's 3,373, a 47-point margin. Harris carried it by 19 points in 2024, so the county moved 27 points toward the Democrats, more than the state's 21-point shift and the typical New Mexico county's 19. It ranks 8th of 33 counties by move, and every county in the state moved left.

Turnout was 12,643 votes, 79% of the 15,989 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Comparable counties moved by similar amounts: Mora by 28 points, McKinley by 33 and San Miguel by 24.

35001.t:
Bernalillo County, New Mexico's largest by votes cast, moved 17 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Ben Luján and Larry Marker. Harris carried it by 21 points in 2024; Luján won it by 38, with 172,306 votes to Marker's 77,461. That is a large swing, but slightly smaller than the typical New Mexico county's move of 19 points, ranking 23rd of 33 in a state where every county moved left. Similar counties swung harder: Rio Arriba by 27 points, Doña Ana by 26 and McKinley by 33.

Turnout fell to 249,767 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35025.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Marker carried Lea County 9,211 to 4,133, a 38-point Republican margin, down from Trump's 62-point margin in 2024. That 24-point move toward the Democrats ranks 11th of New Mexico's 33 counties, all of which moved left, and beats the typical county's 19 points. Luján won statewide by 27. Comparable Republican counties shifted less: Eddy by 17 points, Chaves by 19 and Union by 17.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 13,344 votes, 63% of its 21,209 in 2024. With that many fewer ballots, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35045.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker, San Juan County stayed Republican but by far less than in 2024. Marker won 21,219 votes to Luján's 17,413, an R+10 margin, compared with Trump's R+32 against Harris. That 22-point move toward the Democrats is slightly larger than the state's 21-point swing and the typical New Mexico county's 19, placing San Juan 13th of 33 counties, all of which moved left. Among similar counties, Otero moved 19 points, Torrance 19 and Lincoln 13.

Turnout fell sharply: 38,632 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. About 98% of the expected vote is counted.

35033.t:
Mora County gave Ben Luján a lopsided win in the U.S. Senate race, 1,596 votes to 599 for Larry Marker, a margin of 45 points. In 2024 Kamala Harris carried the county by 17 points, so it moved 28 points toward the Democrats. That is the fourth-largest move among New Mexico's 33 counties, all of which shifted left. The typical county moved 19 points, the state about 21 and the typical county nationally 14. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Rio Arriba 27 points, San Miguel 24 and McKinley 33.

About 2,195 votes were cast, 88% of the 2024 total. With fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35013.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker, Doña Ana County swung about 26 points toward the Democrats. Harris carried it by 10 points in 2024; Luján won it by 35, with 45,139 votes to 21,583. That shift beat the statewide move of 21 points and the typical New Mexico county's 19, ranking ninth of 33 in a state where every county moved left. Among similar counties, Sandoval moved 14 points, Grant 20 and Rio Arriba 27.

Turnout was 66,722 votes, 78% of the 2024 total of 85,407. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. About 98% of the expected vote is counted.

35031.t:
McKinley County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Luján and Marker. Harris carried it by 25 points in 2024; Luján won it by 57, with 15,751 votes to 4,268, a move of 33 points. That was the second-largest swing among New Mexico's 33 counties, all of which moved left, and well above the typical state move of 19 points and the national typical move of 14.

Turnout fell: 20,019 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Rio Arriba moved 27 points, San Miguel 24 and Los Alamos 10. Statewide, Luján won by 27 points, a 21-point move.

35007.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Colfax County went for Luján over Marker by 8 points, 2,561 votes to 2,200, after backing Trump over Harris by 14 points in 2024. That 22-point shift toward the Democrats flipped the county, one of five in New Mexico to go from Trump to the Democrat. Every county in the state moved left. Colfax's move ranks 14th of 33, a little larger than the typical county's 19 points and close to the statewide swing of 21. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

Turnout was 4,761 votes, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Valencia moved 23 points, Sierra 17 and Luna 33.

35029.t:
Luna County voted for Trump by 19 points in 2024 and for Democrat Luján by 14 points in the 2026 U.S. Senate race against Republican Marker, 3,385 votes to 2,558. That 33-point move toward the Democrats is the third-largest among New Mexico's 33 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county moved 19 points and the state about 21. Luna is one of five counties that flipped from Trump to the Democrat. Similar counties moved less: Sierra 17 points, Colfax 22, Valencia 23.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 5,943 votes, 74% of its 2024 total of 8,056. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

35003.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Catron County stayed firmly Republican, but by less than in 2024. Marker beat Luján 1,303 to 635, a margin of about 35 points, down from Trump's 50-point margin over Harris. That is a 16-point move toward the Democrats. It was a little smaller than the typical New Mexico county's 19 points and the state's 21, ranking 26th of 33 counties, all of which moved left. It was slightly larger than the typical national move of 14. Similar small, heavily Republican counties moved alike: Union by 17, Roosevelt by 16, De Baca by 12.

Turnout was 1,938 votes, 82% of the 2,357 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

35009.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Curry County stayed firmly Republican, backing Marker over Luján 6,404 to 3,925, a margin of 24 points. That is a sharp narrowing from Trump's 43-point margin over Harris in 2024, a shift of 19 points toward the Democrats. Only 10,329 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Every New Mexico county moved left. Curry's shift matched the typical county in the state (19 points) and exceeded the typical county nationally (14). Among similar counties, it moved about as much as Chaves (19) and more than Roosevelt (16) and Lincoln (13). Luján won statewide by 27 points.

35023.t:
Hidalgo County flipped in the U.S. Senate race, giving Democrat Luján 741 votes to 683 for Republican Marker, a margin of about 4 points. Trump carried it by 23 in 2024, so the county moved 27 points toward the Democrats. That is more than the typical New Mexico county (19) and the typical county nationally (14). It ranked sixth of 33 in the state by size of move and was one of five to go from Trump to the Democrat.

Turnout was 1,424 votes, 76% of 2024's 1,862, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Luna moved further (33 points), while Sierra (17) and Otero (19) moved less and stayed Republican.

35037.t:
Quay County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by far less than in 2024. Marker beat Luján here 1,727 to 1,060, a margin of 24 points, down from Trump's 41-point win over Harris. That 17-point move toward the Democrats is a little smaller than the typical New Mexico county's 19 points, ranking 22nd of 33, though larger than the typical 14-point move nationally. Among similar strongly Republican counties in the state, Torrance moved 19 points, Roosevelt 16 and Lincoln 13.

Only 2,787 votes were cast, 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
